rows.source: Barsi, Carboni & Lacarbonara (2025), Engineering Structures 323, 119217; DOI 10.1016/j.engstruct.2024.119217; paper_id 9f4295be23
rows.formulation_name: Linearized shear-deformable rope beam with wire eigenstrain limit states
rows.mechanical_object: Short helical single- or multi-strand steel wire rope
state_variables: generalized strain gamma and curvature mu
wire eigenstrain beta^(i) assigned by limit slip state

kinematics.slip: kinematically prescribed perfect-stick, partial-stick and full-slip limits
kinematics.stick_slip_transition: not solved as a local evolving contact law
kinematics.cross_section_deformation: shared rope/wire section rotations; independent section distortion absent

contact_model.normal: no resolved normal-contact law in published limit-state derivation
contact_model.tangential: slip represented by incompatible eigenstrain states
contact_model.coulomb: friction motivates modes, but no full Coulomb traction update or pressure-dependent transition solved
contact_model.normal_force_dependence: qualitative transition rationale, not a calibrated p-to-contact-force law

rows.constitutive_model: Linear elastic E,G wire rods; generalized 6x6 rope stiffness depends on selected slip state.
rows.supports_nonlinear_NiTi: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION: replace wire stress-resultant tangent/update and add transformation state, then rederive consistent rope tangent; constant matrix and closed forms no longer apply.
rows.supports_history: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION for NiTi state; published rope model lacks contact-memory evolution.
rows.supports_pressure_boundary: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION through an added membrane/contact submodel; not published for pressure-controlled rope.
rows.supports_local_observables: Wire strain/resultants by assumed state; no predictive distributed slip/contact traction field.
geometry_assumptions: all wires in one slip state for constant stiffness matrix
known_limitations: published validation concerns upper/lower bending stiffness bounds, not full evolving pressure-controlled hysteresis
perfect-stick bound overestimates measured maximum stiffness in paper
no explicit membrane, transformation, heterogeneous contact topology or finite-deformation solver
required_adaptation: rebuild geometry for straight packed MP1 wires
resolve heterogeneous stick-slip via contact solver if transition curves required
rows.MP1_applicability: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION as diagnostic stiffness bounds, not primary forward H0b
evidence_pointer: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2025-A new mechanical model of short wire ropes Theory and experimental.pdf: abstract; Section 2, Eqs. (1),(2),(6),(7),(11),(12),(18); Section 4
rows.correction_to_worker_record: The prior matrix overstates this as a Coulomb transition predictor. The PDF calls its states kinematic hypotheses and limits its comparison to stiffness bounds.

rows.source: Tjahjanto, Tyrberg & Jonathan Mullins (2017), ASME OMAE2017-62553; paper_id ccdc1bb980; DOI not verified from repository PDF
rows.formulation_name: Geometrically nonlinear 3D component-resolved cable FE plus loxodromic analytical stress comparator
rows.mechanical_object: Three helical power cores, fillers, armour and sheaths in dynamic submarine cable
state_variables: 3D displacement/contact state of each modeled component
external radial pressure and axial strain

kinematics.torsion: component twisting and large rotations in FE
kinematics.stick_slip_transition: Coulomb interface with elastic slip regularization
kinematics.wire_contact: component contact resolved; individual copper conductor wires are not separately resolved in shown cable FE
kinematics.prestrain: specified axial strain and residual-sheath pressure
kinematics.helix: three helical cores; analytical comparator assumes loxodromic slip

contact_model.tangential: Coulomb friction, reported coefficient 0.25 and elastic slip limit 0.001
contact_model.coulomb: friction capacity depends on contact force; analytical Eq. (6): f=mu_o Q_o+mu_i Q_i
contact_model.penalty: normal penalty stated; numerical stiffness not extracted as physical parameter
contact_model.normal_force_dependence: analytical contact forces from axial straining, component tension and radial transmission through structure

rows.constitutive_model: Published FE examples use linear elastic constituent properties.
rows.supports_nonlinear_NiTi: APPLICABLE_WITH_PARAMETERIZATION at constitutive-point level of 3D FE, with a verified NiTi material update.
rows.supports_history: APPLICABLE_WITH_PARAMETERIZATION through constitutive/contact state updates; published material example is elastic.
rows.supports_pressure_boundary: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE as radial traction on outer sheath in FE; published load case uses 0.2 MPa fixed pressure.
rows.supports_wire_slip: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION: resolve actual MP1 individual wires instead of only cable-scale cores/components.
rows.supports_bending: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE in FE; analytical comparator has helical/loxodromic restrictions.
rows.supports_local_observables: FE contact tractions, component stress and slip fields; exact MP1 wire-scale outputs require explicit-wire mesh.
geometry_assumptions: published cable is helical and sheathed
specified axial strain and radial pressure
analytical contact estimate neglects same-layer contact
known_limitations: published numerical study is not pressure-controlled NiTi bundle bending validation
analytical p-to-normal mapping for three-core system is acknowledged insufficient and FE is used
no independent MP1 membrane or wire packing calibration
required_adaptation: replace cable geometry by actual straight packed wires and sleeve
apply chamber pressure to fluid-wetted membrane surface and calibrate transmitted traction
rows.MP1_applicability: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION; main mechanical template for pressure, bending, membrane and resolved contact
evidence_pointer: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/A6-2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf: title page, analytical Eqs. (1)-(6), Analysis Load Case, 3D FE Model
rows.correction_to_worker_record: Repository PDF identifies Jonathan Mullins and OMAE2017-62553; worker row states David Mullins and a different proceeding number/DOI. PDF presents FE-versus-analytical comparison, not a new full-scale bending experiment.

rows.source: Xin Liu (2004), University of Hawaii MSc thesis, Cable Vibration Considering Internal Friction; paper_id aaad9c248c; no DOI verified
rows.formulation_name: 1D transverse cable dynamics with curvature-dependent flexural rigidity supplied by CableCAD
rows.mechanical_object: Multi-layer steel cable idealized as a variable-rigidity continuum beam/cable
state_variables: elementwise EI(kappa) supplied by external CableCAD calculation

kinematics.axial: tension input; elongation neglected in vibration equation
kinematics.slip: represented through EI-curvature input and layer transition estimates
kinematics.stick_slip_transition: not independently resolved by vibration PDE
kinematics.wire_contact: not explicit in 1D PDE; CableCAD uses measured layer pressures
kinematics.cross_section_deformation: warping allowed conceptually, not spatially resolved

contact_model.normal: measured internal layer pressure supplied to CableCAD
contact_model.tangential: static interlayer friction in upstream CableCAD; kinetic friction neglected in stated PDE assumptions
contact_model.coulomb: not an explicit local contact update in thesis 1D solver
contact_model.normal_force_dependence: critical slip curvatures depend on measured layer pressure in CableCAD input

rows.constitutive_model: Published 1D cable assumptions are homogeneous isotropic linear elasticity with EI(kappa) supplied externally.
rows.supports_nonlinear_NiTi: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION only if an independently predicted history-dependent EI(kappa,T,p) is supplied; otherwise risks circular calibration.
rows.supports_history: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE in local contact law; dynamic integration alone does not provide NiTi phase history.
rows.supports_pressure_boundary: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION through external pressure-to-EI/contact solver, not direct 1D traction.
rows.supports_bending: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE for transverse vibration with supplied EI
rows.supports_local_observables: No local contact or transformation fields
known_limitations: cannot independently predict MP1 local slip and transformation signatures
not a journal paper in repository PDF
requires measured layer pressure and external CableCAD closure
required_adaptation: history-aware state update if cyclic response needed
rows.MP1_applicability: NOT_APPLICABLE as strongest stand-alone H0b; useful legacy reduced comparator
evidence_pointer: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/A5-Cable vibration considering internal friction.pdf: title page; Chapter 2 assumptions; Chapter 3 Section 3.2 and CableCAD EI-curvature discussion; Appendix A
rows.correction_to_worker_record: Earlier matrix labels it an ASME journal paper with DOI and explicit local Coulomb model; repository PDF is a 2004 MSc thesis using CableCAD-derived EI.

rows.source: Kang, Wang, Zhou & Xue (2020), Journal of Mechanical Engineering 56(14), 65 onward; DOI 10.3901/JME.2020.14.065; paper_id 56793dea9b
rows.formulation_name: Incremental SMA UMAT with 3D solid FE cable and smooth interwire contact
rows.mechanical_object: 7x7 helical SMA superelastic cable under axial tension
state_variables: shape-memory factor eta / martensite fraction xi
transformation strain and changing elastic modulus

kinematics.bending: not validated in the reported simulations
kinematics.torsion: geometric helix present, torsional response not target
kinematics.slip: frictional slip suppressed by smooth contact

contact_model.penalty: specific method and parameters not verified

rows.constitutive_model: Incremental shape-memory-factor SMA law; transformation-dependent modulus, temperature-dependent thresholds and internal state in UMAT.
rows.supports_history: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE for material transformation history, not contact friction history
rows.supports_pressure_boundary: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION in 3D FE, with a membrane mesh/traction added
rows.supports_wire_slip: NOT_APPLICABLE in reported frictionless implementation; framework can be extended with Coulomb interface
rows.supports_bending: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION in FE, but published validation is tensile
rows.supports_local_observables: Stress/transformation fields available; no frictional slip field in reported setup
known_limitations: reported validation concerns tension, not pressure-controlled bending
repository filename starts 2025 but paper itself is 2020
required_adaptation: introduce frictional contact and mesh verification
model actual MP1 packing and sleeve
rows.MP1_applicability: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION as constitutive/solid FE precedent; insufficient alone for H0b frictional mechanism

rows.source: Vahidi, Arghavani, Choi & Ostadrahimi (published online 2021; corpus file labeled 2022), Mechanics of Advanced Materials and Structures; DOI 10.1080/15376494.2021.1955313; paper_id 53200aa0c6
rows.formulation_name: 3D solid explicit-wire FE with Souza transformation model and interwire friction
rows.mechanical_object: Single- and double-helix SMA wire ropes under axial tension

kinematics.torsion: helical geometry generates torque and shear
kinematics.stick_slip_transition: implicit contact solution, but local transition results not fully specified
kinematics.cross_section_deformation: 3D solid mesh can represent it within discretization

contact_model.normal: surface-to-surface contact; exact normal enforcement and penalty constants not specified in checked text
contact_model.tangential: friction coefficient approximately 0.115 for SMA wires
contact_model.coulomb: frictional contact stated; exact tangential regularization not specified in checked text
contact_model.penalty: not verified in PDF text, so no physical inference from penalty setting
contact_model.normal_force_dependence: computed from geometry/load/contact, not imposed equal to external pressure

rows.constitutive_model: Souza et al. 3D phenomenological thermodynamic SMA law, Eqs. (1)-(8); transformation strain tensor bounded by e_L and temperature-dependent transformation stress; implemented by UMAT.
rows.supports_nonlinear_NiTi: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE at material/contact FE architecture level
rows.supports_history: DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE for transformation internal variable; friction contact history requires solver state verification
rows.supports_pressure_boundary: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION by adding pressurized membrane and external traction
rows.supports_wire_slip: APPLICABLE_WITH_PARAMETERIZATION via frictional surface contact, subject to contact-law verification
rows.supports_bending: APPLICABLE_WITH_BOUNDED_EXTENSION in 3D FE; paper demonstrates tensile response only
rows.supports_local_observables: 3D wire stress and transformation fields; contact gap/slip/traction outputs require explicit extraction and verification
geometry_assumptions: length chosen to reduce clamp effects
known_limitations: no pressure sleeve or active confinement

material parameters adopted from available experiments, not independent MP1 calibration
tension/compression asymmetry neglected in the model

thermal branch if pilots show non-isothermal behavior
